description: Required-row inventory for the M7 family release gate (Tools/ReleaseQualification.py). Every row blocks the release unless a single admissible evidence record passes it. evidenceClass=production rows accept only production-class records on the required build kind; fixture/rehearsal evidence is structurally refused there. evidenceClass=fixture rows qualify pipeline/tooling BEHAVIOR only — they never qualify a package, and the physical/production counterparts remain separate required rows. Rows are derived from the plan's Task 0 dependency table, the Task 6 physical matrix, and the global constraints.

rows.description: The candidate manifest records the source commit, clean-source status, tool versions, gameplay/content fingerprints, and exact per-file SHA-256/size for every shipped file.

The signed APK's aapt badging matches release.json: applicationId com.daniel.familyracing, versionName/versionCode, minSdk 25, targetSdk 36, ARM64 payload, android:debuggable=false, no validation endpoints.
The Windows x64 Mono package is a complete ordinary player (exe + Data + UnityPlayer.dll + Mono runtime), correct company/product identity, no saves/keys/validation tokens inside.
The APK bundles the complete offline inventory: every course, font, translation, sound and voice prompt; arcade backend; works with no internet.
The Windows ZIP bundles the complete offline inventory: every course, font, translation, sound and voice prompt; arcade backend; works with no internet.
Third-party notices and required license/attribution text are bundled in both packages and complete for the shipped content; costs recorded.
apksigner verify --print-certs on the shipped APK reports signer #1 certificate SHA-256 equal to release.json expectedCertificateSha256 (v2/v3 signature scheme).

The family release key is owner-controlled: the owner has located and recovered the keystore backup to a clean location and re-verified the certificate fingerprint; no secret material exists in tracked files or logs.
M4 acceptance on the SM-T220 (3 GB): real lightmap bake, owner visual approval, both vehicle classes and both cameras, A7 Lite hosting four racers, sustained render + memory evidence.

M5 first world exists and is family-reviewed: two authored Sunny Island courses, 26 events, runtime CourseLoader/GameplayLoopSetup binding; authored-content scenario rows verified on the authored build.
M6 production content is bound into the shipped build: three worlds, six courses, eight models, 78 authored events with real per-event objectives/rewards, liveries/rivals, contentStage complete.

Matching development builds pass the production scopes: all 78 events and each course/class Quick Race + Time Trial combination with correct objectives/rewards, LAN scope, generation-2 memory samples after rejoin, M6 pacing evidence, inherited command/state reconstruction checks.
Final reviewed English and Hebrew audio: the 9 tutorial cues and the 14 production prompts in both locales, generated under credential and listened-to by a reviewer.
Inherited M1-M3 device/human acceptance folded into the physical matrix: install, real touch input, on-device feel review, and LAN acceptance on ordinary packages.
Matched-workload instrumentation-overhead A/B comparison separates development instrumentation cost from ordinary-package performance, on PC and on device.
Fresh install of the shipped APK on a tablet with no internet: launches, completes tutorial and representative content, bundled fonts/audio work, settings and progress survive a restart.
Fresh extraction of the shipped ZIP on a PC with no internet: launches, completes tutorial and representative content, bundled fonts/audio work, settings and progress survive a restart.

LAN hosting permutations on ordinary packages over disconnected-internet Wi-Fi: tablet-to-tablet without PC, tablet-to-PC with each hosting, four physical devices including the A7 Lite as host, and a PC host.

Join failure paths on ordinary packages: permission denial where applicable, blocked discovery, manual-IP fallback, full lobby, unreachable host, incompatible gameplay/content builds — each with a useful bilingual recovery.
Session recovery on ordinary packages: disconnect during countdown, race, pause, finish and result delivery; reconnect ownership/AI attribution; host loss; no duplicate or aborted rewards.
Impaired Wi-Fi on ordinary packages: normal baseline plus measured/injected 100 ms RTT, +/-30 ms jitter and 2% loss, with no routine large visible correction jumps.

At least 30 racing minutes (measured racing time, not uptime) on the ordinary package with the A7 Lite hosting: both classes/cameras, rematches and course switches, profile switching, application restarts; thermal slowdown and memory growth inspected.
rows.source: Task 6 physical matrix: sustained ordinary play

rows.description: At least 30 racing minutes on the ordinary package with the PC hosting under the same scenario mix; thermal and memory behavior inspected.
rows.source: Task 6 physical matrix: sustained ordinary play

rows.description: SM-T220 performance on the ordinary package: 95th-percentile steady-state frame time at or below 40 ms, 30 fps target, no recurring stalls above 100 ms, within the 800 MB process-memory budget; actual measurements and all deviations reported.
rows.source: Task 6 physical matrix: performance; global budget

rows.description: PC performance on the ordinary package: 60 fps at 1080p; actual measurements and deviations reported.

On a real install: progress earned through normal gameplay in all four slots, then the newer same-signer APK installed over the predecessor; all four profiles survive with semantic state and retained receipts (no double rewards). OPEN: requires hardware + ordinary packages; the fixture rehearsal only proves tooling mechanics.
On the shipped Windows package: progress in all four slots, then binaries replaced while LocalLow data is preserved; all four profiles survive with receipts intact.

On each supported tablet with the ordinary APK: discover the real profile data location and qualify scoped adb pull/push backup plus restore round-trip, including automatic .bak recovery. No root or run-as assumption.
On the shipped Windows package's real LocalLow store: automatic .bak recovery plus an external same-installation backup/restore round-trip on all four slots.

On a real device: an APK signed by a mismatched signer or carrying a non-increasing version code is rejected at install time and the existing install plus its data remain usable. OPEN: requires hardware; tooling-level rejection is proven separately.

Ordinary input and presentation on real devices: real keyboard/touch, simultaneous and held input, focus loss/recovery, both cameras, reduced shake, volume and replay controls, English/Hebrew layout and voice review.
On the ordinary packages: no validation listeners or tokens exist even when validation arguments are supplied; endpoints are compiled out by construction and verified at runtime.
rows.source: Task 6 physical matrix; global development-contract constraint

rows.description: The shipped Windows ZIP extracted to a clean location and launched offline under a separate clean Windows account without Unity installed; profiles/settings land in the established per-user LocalLow path and all content is accessible under its unlock rules.
rows.source: M7 Task 3 open row; Task 6 qualification

rows.description: A five-year-old on the ordinary package completes onboarding, identifies controls, finishes the introductory race, understands the reward, and starts another event with little reading help; assistance, readability, touch issues, camera comfort, enjoyment and voluntary replay recorded.
A Hebrew-speaking reviewer checks RTL layout, mixed numbers/IP fields, complete text, and every voice prompt on the ordinary package.
The owner reviews visual and audio quality on the A7 Lite ordinary build, including pronunciation.
rows.source: Task 6 family sessions; M4 owner review

rows.description: Family pacing playtests on the ordinary package measure campaign duration and enjoyment; duration is measured racing time, not process uptime.
rows.source: Task 6 family sessions; M6 pacing evidence

rows.description: A parent follows the shipped guides on ordinary devices end-to-end: verify/download from the private location, install or update, start offline, host/join, permit private-network firewall access without disabling the firewall, recover a failed join, back up and recover progress.

The separate migration path for debug-signed predecessors is documented in the backup/install guides (preserve saves, test before removal); no silent uninstall and no claim of release-key continuity over debug installs.

TOOLING row (fixture evidence allowed): a same-test-key fixture APK pair with distinct increasing version codes proves signer-continuity/update mechanics at pipeline level — apksigner reports one identical certificate and version codes increase. Explicitly labeled rehearsal; never an upgrade from a shipped version.

TOOLING row (fixture evidence allowed): replacing a disposable Windows install's binaries while preserving a disposable LocalLow Profiles tree leaves every profile byte identical — the Windows update mechanic at fixture level.

TOOLING row (fixture evidence allowed): the signing pipeline refuses an APK whose signer certificate does not match the expected SHA-256 and publishes nothing. Physical install rejection stays open under physical.install-rejection.

TOOLING row (fixture evidence allowed): the pipeline rejects a release whose androidVersionCode is not strictly above the declared predecessor (FamilyReleaseSettings.Validate/Apply plus manifest identity checks).
TOOLING row (fixture evidence allowed): unreadable or newer-schema profile files are preserved, never silently overwritten, across update/backup/restore paths (ProfileStore + backup tool contract).
rows.source: Task 5 negative cases; global save-preservation constraint

rows.description: TOOLING row (fixture evidence allowed): a rejected or interrupted operation leaves the existing installation usable — failed signing publishes nothing, an aborted restore leaves pre-restore bytes and a resumable/rollbackable journal.
rows.source: Task 5 negative cases; Task 4 journal contract

rows.description: TOOLING row (fixture evidence allowed): the backup/restore tools round-trip all profile bytes identically against the real Windows LocalLow profile layout with rehearsal profiles, and the tooling suite proves every failure class.

TOOLING row (fixture evidence allowed): the Android backup/restore contract — serial checks, scoped Android/data path, running-game detection, atomic push, journal — exercised against a simulated device filesystem. The physical on-device row stays separate and open.
rows.source: Task 4 tooling (Android arm unqualified on hardware)
